title: Wilhelm cracks the ritual integration over the winter
notes: Wilhelm's winter work at Carrick: the folk system stops being spontaneous-only. He judges the formulaic-ritual step 'really easy — someone just needed to point it out'; the remaining work is formalizing the Artes Liberales / Philosophiae contribution.
source: Session recap 2026-07-25 (Ars Magica transcript), winter-1223 downtime.
body_text:
Wintering at **Carrick** while his research assistants are out gathering material, Wilhelm spends the season on **integration and research** — turning his folk system from a curiosity into something with proper mechanics.
**The breakthrough he's most confident about:** his current system knows only **spontaneous, ritual-style casting** (roll halved). Proper **formulaic** magic would let a caster add **Artes Liberales** and **Philosophiae** to the effort *and* drop the divide-by-two — roughly tripling the effective pool. Over the winter he works out that this ritual integration is, in his own estimate, **"really easy — someone just needed to point it out"**: give a caster the finished formula rather than making them improvise it each time.
**The Artes Liberales angle** is the part still taking his time: the obvious-once-said refinements a folk caster never bothered to name. If a ceremony wants a circle, it helps to know **geometry** enough to draw a true one; if it wants words of power, it helps to know **rhetoric** enough to project the voice. Formalizing how Artes Liberales and Philosophiae feed the working is the winter's real labor.
**Logistics.** His assistants are sent west and south to gather hedge-magic insight, carrying **sacks of grain and silver** as payment for anyone willing to teach the "easy stuff." Wilhelm writes letters — to the loose **wizard-circle** he keeps looped in on the project, to his family, and to **Dietrich** (his brother/scribe, back at his teaching post), whom he promises a **tractatus of the generated folk-magic spells** once it's finished. He intends to set up a **lab on shore** (he is chronically seasick and will not stay aboard ship an hour longer than he must), and has arranged for his research materials to be relocated from home toward wherever the covenant next bases itself. Feeds t019, t009, and the mundane vis-factory pitch (t020).

title: The covenant's Isle-of-Man base revealed: Ránargarðr, Nóatún, and Undrahöll
notes: Isle-of-Man buildout + the Winter 1221-22 covenant vote narrated to set up the Spring 1224 arrival. Owner-confirmed: the ~40£ structure cost is PART OF the 100£ total in holdings.json (structure + tools), not a contradiction; the site carries a MAGIC aura of 3 as recorded, but its source has not yet been described in play (U1 open on source only). Site = Laxey, east coast.
body_text:
Backstory set at the table: over Winters 1221–22 Valdemar tired of the covenant wintering expensively in Bruges and pitched an anchorage of the covenant's own. In Summer 1222 he surveyed the Isle of Man — largely ill-ruled, Norse-claimed — and chose a harbour site he named **Ránargarðr**.
Valdemar brought a formal proposal (Winter 1221–22): seek the local Norse lord's permission rather than run a pirate's cove; ~50 Mythic pounds to start (of a ~130£ full estimate — 5£ quarters per magus, 1£ per grog family, plus construction).
The magi debated: Dagmar wary of tying resources to a stationary site (the covenant is deliberately mobile) unless it sits on a strong aura; Éogan for it if it pays its way; all agreed it must generate income, not be a financial sink.
Peripheral-Code note raised in play: magi may not swear fealty or serve as court wizards, but may hold a landed site; the Isle of Man is a jurisdictional grey zone — not the Normandy Tribunal, not clearly any Tribunal (a feature Valdemar sought).
By Spring 1224 the base is built out (not fully finished): a Norse-style settlement of longhouses and local stone at **Laxey** (east coast), on a Magic-aura site (GM: 'R3'), with a slipway to haul ships, fields sown, and grog families settled.
The great hall **Nóatún** ('place of ships') is where the coven winters. Above it on a promontory rises Valdemar's laboratory-hall **Undrahöll** — a single ~4,500 sq ft longhouse that dwarfs Nóatún, seaside-facing for the idyllic-surroundings benefit, with the working lab walled off in a chamber for Safety.
Funding: Valdemar has committed to piracy to help pay for it. The lab structure runs ~40£; the expensive tool/equipment upgrades drive the total far higher, while Safety is held at 0 by design.

title: Rembrandt DeWeese made custos; Wilhelm's grain-dish installed
notes: Which associate installs the dish (Isaac vs Carl) left open at the table. The dish is on loan, not gifted.
body_text:
The base needs a mundane custos/majordomo. **Rembrandt DeWeese** — formerly captain of the Brineborn under Éogan, and before that a soldier/bodyguard and merchant-in-training aboard the Tide of Memory under Solving — is promoted to run Ránargarðr; his first mate steps up to captain the Brineborn.
Wilhelm's associate (Isaac or Carl) offers to install Wilhelm's magical grain dish — a Dish of Plenty holding a vast store of grain but pourable only slowly (~2 pawns to invoke) — in a storehouse to help feed the community.
Legal caveat noted in play: the conjured grain can't be sold, only lived on. Left here on loan for a season or more, as a favour.

title: Wilhelm invited to formalize covenant membership
body_text:
With seven magi official plus Wilhelm (Solving absent, Kor on hiatus), Dustin offers Wilhelm — a fellow ex Bonisagus — full membership, explicitly on his merits and not for his grain dish.
Wilhelm gives a tentative yes: the Isle of Man is a fine research base (Ireland's and England's natural traditions), but his commitment depends on where his research leads. He'll keep the dish here on loan regardless.

title: Regiones the Third: the frog-folk ambush (cliffhanger)
notes: s16 reached (cliffhanger). The murfolk (frog-folk) confirmed as the Level-3 colony. Session ended here; next session opens on the ambush.
body_text:
Crossing into Level 3: a bioluminescent marsh — fungi above and below the water, paths that dip between deep pools, and **underwater 'homesteads'** framed in light, with figures moving in the depths.
An arrow lands at Garrett's feet; a dart strikes Dagmar's neck and drops him into a hallucinatory (not unconscious) state. As he goes under he locks eyes with the shooter — not a merman like Ka'wa'ill but a grotesque, intelligent **frog-fish person** (the murfolk).
Ambush sprung; the scene is paused here — next session opens on dealing with it.
